docs.title: Instructions
docs.text: Our primary objective: move keyforge from a barely working prototype to a well factored, well architected application that delivers an excellent user experience. A world class production quality application. ... I have provide two files that contain the current state of the keyforge application code. I have not included data but I can provide it if need. Our first task is tasks missing from the current plan to achieve our objective. I want you to identify all the actors engaging with keyforge application or code. I want you to identify all requirements FURPS+ and I want a complete list of tasks that addresses their needs that are not currently listed in the plan. Our current plan is in docs/theplan.md.

docs.title: Prompt
docs.text:
SYSTEM PROMPT: KEYFORGE CORE

GLOBAL CONTEXT You are KeyForge Core, an elite systems engineering unit. Your Goal: Engineering Truth. Your Enemy: Latency, Memory Allocation, Token Waste, Tunnel Vision, and Scope Creep.

  1. THE COUNCIL (FUNCTIONAL PERSONAS) Activate these modules dynamically based on the task. [VIKTOR] Architect: Enforces O(n), cache locality. "Memory allocation is a failure of planning." [ELENA] Biomechanics: Optimizes SFB, DSFB. "Data doesn't feel pain, the user does." [MORGAN] QA & Cycle Breaker: Adversarial tester. "If we tried this twice, it's wrong." Detects loops. [ALEX] Implementation: Idiomatic Code. "If the compiler fights you, the design is wrong." [SOLON] Research: Search Topology & Math. Simulates High-Temperature lateral thinking. [ELIAS] UX: Flow state & Data Viz. [MARCUS] SRE: Observability & Security. "You cannot fix what you cannot see."

  2. THE OPERATIONAL PROTOCOL (MANDATORY) You must adhere to a strict Request-Plan-Execute cycle.

PHASE 1: COGNITIVE TRACE (Internal Monologue) 1. Deconstruct: Break the request into atomic constraints. 2. Input Validation: - Is the user input Source Code or an Error Log? DO NOT ASSUME. - If ambiguous, ask for clarification before diagnosing. 3. Cycle Check: - If the proposed strategy matches a previous failed attempt: STOP. - Trigger [SOLON] for a Lateral Shift. 4. Scope Lock: - Identify EXACTLY which files are requested. - Listing unrequested files is a PROTOCOL VIOLATION.

PHASE 2: THE BLUEPRINT (The Response) Output the Engineering Strategy. Structure: [SITREP]: Current System Status. [MORGAN AUDIT]: Status (PASS/FAIL). Root Cause. Verdict. [VIKTOR STRATEGY]: The algorithmic fix. [ALEX MANIFEST]: - File: src/path/to/file.rs - Action: (Modify / Create / Delete) - Rationale: Why this specific change? [PERMISSION GATE]: - STOP. Do not generate code. - Ask: "Blueprint ready. Shall I fabricate [Specific File]?"

PHASE 3: FABRICATION (Triggered by User Command) Constraint: Permission is TRANSACTIONAL. Approval to dump main.rs DOES NOT grant permission to dump lib.rs. Constraint: Output ONLY the requested file(s). Constraint: When generating a file, provide the FULL FILE LISTING unless >300 lines.

  1. THE IRONCLAD CONSTRAINTS (OVERRIDE)
  2. THE PRESERVATION MANDATE: You are FORBIDDEN from deleting logic blocks to fix compilation errors unless the logic is proven dead. You must fix the Type Mismatch, not delete the Consumer.
  3. THE SCOPE LOCK: If the user asks for "poison_pill.rs", providing "sync.rs" is a failure.

  4. THE OBSERVABILITY RULE: If a fix fails once, you are FORBIDDEN from attempting a code fix in the next turn. You must generate Instrumentation (Logs/Asserts) to prove the state.

  5. INTERACTION STYLE Tone: Professional, terse, engineering-focused. Visuals: Use ASCII grids (3x10) for layout analysis. Reasoning: Chain of Thought is mandatory.

  6. USER CONFIGURATION NOTES (Internal)

  7. Phase 1 (Planning): Simulate Temp 0.4 (High Creativity/Constraint Synthesis).
  8. Phase 3 (Coding): Simulate Temp 0.0 (Deterministic/Syntactic Precision).

docs.title: KeyForge Future Roadmap (v1.1+)
docs.text: Status: Future Scope Objective: Features identified as valuable but out of scope for the v1.0 "Operation Ironclad" MVP.

docs.title: 1. Cloud & Community
docs.text:
• Authentication: Google/GitHub OAuth sign-in for Hive.
  • Leaderboards: Global high scores for layouts based on standard corpora.
  • Cloud Sync: Sync user layouts, history, and biometric profiles across devices.

docs.title: 2. Advanced Operations
docs.text:
• Admin Console: Web-based dashboard to monitor Hive health, active agents, job queues, and exceptions.
  • Failover: Multi-server Hive deployment with database replication.
  • Telemetry: Centralized exception logging and usage insights (Opt-in).

docs.title: 3. Web Platform
docs.text:
• Web Frontend: A pure web version of the UI (WASM-based or talking to a public Hive) to allow users to design without installing software.
  • Vial.rocks Integration: Deep linking or compatibility with web-based configurators.

docs.title: 4. Hardware Integration
docs.text:
• QMK/ZMK Export: Generate firmware source files (keymap.c, .keymap) directly from the optimized layout.
  • 3D Model Visualization: Render the keyboard geometry in 3D (Cosmos standard?).

docs.title: 5. Advanced Algorithms
docs.text:
• Splay Assumptions: Advanced physics modeling for splayed keyboards.
  • Population Diversity: Algorithms to ensure the genetic pool maintains diversity rather than converging too early.

docs.title: Operation Ironclad: KeyForge Master Execution Plan (v8.0)
docs.text: Status: Definitive Objective: Transform KeyForge from a functional prototype into a world-class, production-grade Distributed Genetic Optimization System. Architect: KeyForge Core

docs.title: PHASE 1: FOUNDATION & HYGIENE (The Cleanup)
docs.text:
Goal: Fix architectural violations, race conditions, and ensure the application boots reliably on a fresh machine. Zero Silent Failures.

ID Task Persona Description 1.1 Unify I/O Logic (The Split Brain) ALEX Move ui/src-tauri/src/sync_engine.rs logic into crates/keyforge-workspace. Crucial: Implement RwLock on SessionState to prevent cmd_sync_data writing while Scorer reads. 1.2 Native Asset Bootstrapper ELIAS Implement download_essentials() in keyforge-workspace. UI must trigger this on startup if data/ is missing to prevent crash-on-launch. 1.3 Golden Master Regression Suite MORGAN Create a test set of 100 layouts with known scores. Verify "Poison Pill" penalties are clamped (e.g., 1M instead of 1B) to prevent integer overflow. 1.4 Remove Silent Failures (Test Suite) MORGAN Modify: crates/keyforge-core/tests/system/parity.rs -> Replace early returns with panic!. Modify: crates/keyforge-core/tests/system/data_integrity.rs -> Add count tracking and assertions to ensure loop actually ran. 1.5 Embedded Constants Audit VIKTOR Scan codebase for hardcoded paths (/usr/local/...) or magic numbers. Move them to Config structs or const definitions. 1.6 Dependency Audit VIKTOR Remove reqwest from keyforge-ui. Purge --secret CLI args in favor of HIVE_SECRET env vars. Enforce "Protocol only imports types" rule. 1.7 Phase 1 Acceptance MORGAN cargo check --workspace passes. UI boots on fresh machine without manual scripts. Regression suite passes.

docs.title: PHASE 2: DATA INTEGRITY & OPS (The Spine)
docs.text:
Goal: Protect user data and ensure the server can evolve without wiping the database.

ID Task Persona Description 2.1 SQLx Migrations & JSONB MARCUS Replace schema.sql with versioned sqlx migrate files. Refactor scoring_profiles to use a JSONB column for weights to allow dynamic physics updates without schema changes. 2.2 CI/CD Pipeline MARCUS Set up GitHub Actions for cargo test, clippy, and npm run build. Ensure no broken code merges to main. 2.3 Agent Circuit Breaker ALEX Implement logic in keyforge-agent to track failure counts per Job ID. Blacklist Job if it causes >3 panics/errors. 2.4 Input Sanitization Layer MARCUS Implement validate() trait in keyforge-protocol. Reject loader_trigram_limit > 50,000 and malformed geometry to prevent Node OOMs. 2.5 API Rate Limiting MARCUS Add tower-governor middleware to keyforge-hive to prevent DoS via the /jobs and /results endpoints.

docs.title: PHASE 3: THE ENGINE ROOM (Performance & Personalization)
docs.text:
Goal: Maximize optimization efficiency and enable user-specific customization.

ID Task Persona Description 3.1 Unified Statistics (Rust Port) ALEX Port statistical math from TS (ui/services/stats.ts) to Rust (keyforge-core). Expose cmd_get_layout_stats. Prerequisite for 3.2. 3.2 Cost Matrix Generator SOLON Create command to read user_stats.json and generate personal_cost.csv. Allows optimizer to design for specific user finger speeds. we are here ===> 3.3 Scorer LRU Cache SOLON Implement Arc<Scorer> caching in Agent based on config hash. Prevent rebuilding lookup tables for every job in a batch. 3.4 Zero-Allocation Parsing ALEX Refactor layout_string_to_u16 to write to a pre-allocated &mut [u16] buffer instead of returning Vec. 3.5 Implement CompactPosMap SOLON Replace Box<[u8; 65536]> with [u8; 256] in the hot scoring loop to fit in L1 Cache. 3.6 SIMD Safety Implementation ALEX Flesh out evolve_batch_avx2. Critical: Remove unwrap() calls inside hot paths to prevent panics on misaligned data. 3.7 Fuzz Testing Core Parser MORGAN Run cargo-fuzz against the Scorer and Layout Parser to ensure the new Zero-Alloc/SIMD logic is memory safe.

docs.title: PHASE 4: THE HIVE MIND (Operations)
docs.text:
Goal: Operational maturity and ecosystem health.

ID Task Persona Description 4.1 Job Lifecycle Manager MARCUS Add expires_at to DB. Implement background task in Hive to cull zombie jobs. 4.2 Distributed Tracing MARCUS Add trace_id to Protocol. Pass UUID from UI -> Hive -> Agent -> Logs. Enable debugging of distributed failures. 4.3 Log Management MARCUS Implement structured logging (JSON) for Hive and Agent. Ensure logs rotate and do not consume infinite disk space.

docs.title: PHASE 5: THE INTERFACE (UX & Polish)
docs.text:
Goal: Make the tool usable by non-engineers. Fix broken features.

ID Task Persona Description 5.1 CRUD Operations ELIAS Implement full Create/Read/Update/Delete for Keyboards, Layouts, and Corpora in the UI. 5.2 Corpus Manager UI ELIAS Drag-and-drop UI to ingest .txt files into custom N-gram profiles (e.g., "Coding", "Academic"). 5.3 Fix Import/Export VIKTOR Repair broken JSON import/export. Ensure it validates schema versioning. 5.4 Fix Compare UI ELIAS The "Compare" button currently does nothing. Implement side-by-side Diff View (Heatmap Delta). 5.5 WebSocket Purity ELIAS Refactor ui/src/App.tsx to stop polling GET /queue. Listen for WS JOB_UPDATE events for real-time feedback. 5.6 Optimistic UI Pattern ELIAS Implement local state prediction in React to prevent "Jitter" while waiting for Rust backend calculations. 5.7 Integrated Help (MkDocs) ELIAS Embed the documentation site (or a lightweight version) directly into the app via a Help overlay.

docs.title: PHASE 6: LAUNCH READINESS (Distribution)
docs.text:
Goal: Distribution, lifecycle management, and final audit.

ID Task Persona Description 6.1 Installer & Auto-Update MARCUS Configure tauri.conf.json for updates. Build installers (.msi, .dmg, .deb). 6.2 AppImage Fix MARCUS Fix Linux packaging issues. Ensure shared libraries are bundled correctly. 6.3 Onboarding Flow ELIAS Create a "Welcome" modal sequence that guides the user to load a keyboard and run their first analysis. 6.4 Arena Feedback Loop ELIAS Expose mostNeeded bigrams in the Arena UI so users understand why they are typing specific words. 6.5 Final System Audit MORGAN Full regression pass. Documentation generation. Binary signing.

docs.title: KeyForge Architecture Definition
docs.text:
Version: 2.0 (Operation Ironclad) Status: Approved Architect: Viktor Petrov

This document defines the physical and logical boundaries of the KeyForge ecosystem. It adheres to Hexagonal Architecture (Ports and Adapters) principles to ensure the core domain logic remains isolated from infrastructure concerns.

docs.title: 1. Logical Architecture (The "Onion")
docs.text:
Dependencies flow inward. The outer layers depend on the inner layers. The inner layers define interfaces that the outer layers must implement.

      +---------------------------------------------------------------+
      |                    THE APPLICATION LAYER                      |
      | (Drivers, IO, State Management, Networking, Rendering)        |
      |                                                               |
      |  +-------------+    +--------------+    +--------------+      |
      |  | keyforge-ui |    | keyforge-cli |    | keyforge-hive|      |
      |  | (Tauri App) |    | (Command Line)|   | (Server/API) |      |
      |  +------+------+    +-------+------+    +-------+------+      |
      |         |                   |                   |             |
      +---------|-------------------|-------------------|-------------+
                |                   |                   |
      +---------v-------------------v-------------------v-------------+
      |                  THE ADAPTER LAYER                            |
      |           (keyforge-workspace / keyforge-agent)               |
      |                                                               |
      |   [File I/O]      [Http Client]      [DB Access (Hive)]       |
      |   [Caching]       [Telemetery]       [Auth Middleware]        |
      +-----------------------------+---------------------------------+
                                    |
      +-----------------------------v---------------------------------+
      |                   THE CORE DOMAIN                             |
      |                   (keyforge-core)                             |
      |                                                               |
      |    +-----------+    +-----------+    +-----------+            |
      |    | Context   |--->|  Scorer   |<---| Evolution |            |
      |    | (Builder) |    | (Physics) |    | (Genetic) |            |
      |    +-----------+    +-----------+    +-----------+            |
      |                                                               |
      +-----------------------------+---------------------------------+
                                    |
      +-----------------------------v---------------------------------+
      |                 THE SHARED PROTOCOL                           |
      |                 (keyforge-protocol)                           |
      |                                                               |
      |   [DTOs]  [Validators]  [Config Structs]  [Constants]         |
      +---------------------------------------------------------------+

Architectural Constraints: 1. Protocol: Pure Data. No logic. No I/O. 2. Core: Pure Logic. No HTTP. No Database. No println!. 3. Adapters: Handles "How to get data". (Read disk, fetch URL). 4. Apps: Handles "When to do what". (User clicked button -> run job).

docs.title: 2. Physical Topology (Deployment)
docs.text: KeyForge supports a Hybrid Topology: Local execution for privacy/latency, and Distributed execution for massive scale.

docs.title: Scenario B: The Distributed Cluster (Production)
docs.text:
Used for massive search campaigns and community sharing.

                                     +------------------+
                                     |  Postgres DB     |
                                     | (Job/Result Store)|
                                     +--------+---------+
                                              ^
                                              | TCP:5432
+-----------------------+            +--------v---------+
| WORKSTATION (Client)  |            |  CLOUD SERVER    |
|                       |  HTTP/REST |  (keyforge-hive) |
|  [keyforge-ui] ------------------->|                  |
|  (Orchestrator)       |            |  [Job Queue]     |
|                       |            |  [Result Agg]    |
+-----------------------+            +---+----^---------+
                                         |    |
                              WebSocket  |    |  WebSocket
                              (Push Job) |    | (Push Result)
                                         v    |
                            +-----------------+-----------------+
                            |                                   |
                  +---------v----------+              +---------v----------+
                  | COMPUTE NODE A     |              | COMPUTE NODE B     |
                  | (keyforge-agent)   |              | (keyforge-agent)   |
                  | [AVX2 Hot Path]    |              | [AVX2 Hot Path]    |
                  +--------------------+              +--------------------+

docs.title: A. The Core Contract (Rust Native)
docs.text:
Interaction: UI/CLI -> Core

Input:  ContextLoader (Root Path, Keyboard Name, Corpus Config)
Action: Scorer::new() -> Validates & Pre-calculates Tables (300ms)
        Verifier::score(LayoutString) -> ScoreDetails (0.1ms)
        Optimizer::run(Config) -> Layout (Seconds/Minutes)
Output: ValidationResult { Score, Heatmap, Violations }

docs.title: B. The Hive Protocol (HTTP/REST)
docs.text:
Interaction: UI -> Hive Server

POST /jobs
  Payload: RegisterJobRequest (Geometry + Weights + Constraints)
  Response: { "job_id": "uuid", "status": "queued" }

GET /jobs/{id}/population
  Response: { "layouts": ["qwerty...", "colemak..."] }

POST /results
  Payload: SubmitResultRequest (JobId + Layout + Score)
  Response: 200 OK (If verified) / 400 Bad Request (If drift detected)

docs.title: C. The Agent Protocol (WebSocket)
docs.text:
Interaction: Hive <-> Node

(Handshake)
Client -> Server: RegisterNodeRequest { CPU: "AMD Ryzen", Ops: 50M/s }

(Loop)
Server -> Client: { "type": "JOB_AVAILABLE", "id": "uuid" }
Client -> Server: GET /jobs/queue -> JobConfig
Client -> Server: (Optimizes locally...)
Client -> Server: POST /results -> { Layout, Score }

docs.title: 4. Component Responsibility Matrix
docs.text: Component Responsibility Forbidden Actions Protocol Defines types (RegisterJobRequest), Defaults (ScoringWeights), Validators. Logic, I/O, State. Core Physics calc, N-gram stats, Search algorithms, Layout generation. Networking, Thread management, App State. Workspace Finding data/, Downloading files, Caching, Atomic Writes. Optimization logic. Agent Hardware detection, Thread pooling, Server communication loop. Storing persistent results (stateless). Hive Job queue, Result verification, Persistence (DB), Auth. Heavy compute (delegates to Agents). UI Interactive Visualization, Session Management, Local Config. Direct DB access (must use API).

docs.title: 5. Data Flow: The Life of an Optimization
docs.text:
1. Definition: User in UI selects "Corne", "English", and "Low SFB Weights".
  2. Assembly: UI passes this to ContextLoader (Core) to verify files exist locally.
  3. Dispatch: UI sends RegisterJobRequest (Protocol) to Hive.
  4. Distribution: Hive broadcasts "Job Available" via WebSocket.
  5. Acquisition: Agent downloads the specific Corpus/Weights from Hive (via keyforge-workspace).
  6. Optimization: Agent runs Replica::evolve (Core/AVX2) in a loop.
  7. Submission: Agent posts best layout to Hive.
  8. Verification: Hive runs Verifier (Core) to confirm the score matches the layout.
  9. Visualization: UI polls Hive, gets the new layout, and uses Scorer (Core) to render the Heatmap.

docs.text:

Next Steps (The Plan) To align with this architecture, the specific next steps (Phase 2) are: Create crates/keyforge-workspace: Move the file downloading, hashing, and path resolution logic here. Refactor Consumers: Make keyforge-node, keyforge-cli, and keyforge-ui use keyforge-workspace to find their data.
